assumptions: Monte Carlo under an assumed independent-flip judge model, not a theorem about real evaluators.
attrs.evidence: At p = 1% the certificate issues about 5% of the time; at p = 5% essentially never. Majority-of-m judging restores it (p = 5%, m = 9 → ~99%). So the sample budget must declare judges-per-task alongside n, or η must absorb p.

evidence_qualifiers.population: Monte Carlo over an assumed independent-flip judge model at n = 300 per trial; NOT a sample of real evaluators.

attrs.statement: A single judge flipping comparisons at rate p ≥ η makes the zero-violation certificate essentially unattainable at n ≈ 300, even when domination genuinely holds.
